newsitem.title: USA: Summers says EMU no threat to dollar's global role.
newsitem.headline: Summers says EMU no threat to dollar's global role.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Deputy Secretary Lawrence Summers on Thursday said Europe's proposed single currency should be backed by sound economic fundamentals, adding he was not concerned it would undermine the dollar's role in global markets.

"We do not share the concern that ... a new European currency would be a major threat to the dollar's role in the international system and in some way would do damage to America's interests," Summers said.
"We believe it would of course be important for any new currency, just as any old currency, that it be backed by sound macroeconomic fundamentals," Summers said.
Summers reiterated that the United States would like to see Europe pursue policies to restore economic and employment growth in Europe, regardless of the outcome of the single currency drive.

"The greatest concern I think that I would have is to ensure that these debates do not divert the discussion in Europe from what I think is the profoundly important task of creating a regulatory framework and a legal framework in general that is more flexible and is conducive to the restoration of employment growth and economic growth," Summers added.
